comparison: Both strongly support that growth defects in emc mutants are rescued by caspase mutations (C58-C64, C71-C72, C13). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis, while peer reviewers describe findings as 'compelling' and 'convincingly presented.' Complete agreement on this core finding.

Both support that accelerated furrow phenotype in emc mutants is rescued by caspase mutations (C80-C83, C6). OpenEval quantifies rescue percentages (75% for dronc, complete for Df(3L)H99), while peer reviewers accept this as key evidence for non-apoptotic caspase functions. Full agreement.

Both support that R7 and cone cell specification defects in emc mutants are caspase-dependent (C165-C169, C7-C8). OpenEval provides quantification (90% R7 rescue), while peer reviewers accept these as part of comprehensive demonstration of caspase-dependent phenotypes. Complete agreement.

Both support reduced Diap1 in emc mutants (C91-C94, C89). OpenEval notes caution about interpretation and lack of wild-type comparisons, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic link without challenging the distinction between Diap1 levels versus activity. Agreement with OpenEval expressing more nuance.

OpenEval R4 addresses genetic rescue via Diap1/P35 overexpression (C96-C97, C100), while peer R5 addresses both rescue experiments and non-apoptotic nature (C96-C97, C100-C104, C106-C108, C172-C173). Peer reviewers emphasize non-apoptotic caspase activity as key finding. Overlapping claims with peer review covering broader scope.

OpenEval R5 focuses on evidence for non-apoptotic caspase activity via TUNEL/Dcp1 staining and pie mutant controls (C101-C107, C172-C173). Peer R5 accepts non-apoptotic nature and rescue experiments more broadly. Both strongly support the same conclusion with overlapping but not identical claim sets.

Both support that elevated E(spl) in emc mutants is caspase-dependent and that Notch signaling is epistatic to caspases (C144-C145, C149-C151, C9). OpenEval details genetic epistasis with psn mutation, while peer reviewers accept Notch as the target pathway. Complete agreement.

Both support caspase-dependent elevation of Delta protein in emc mutants (C152-C156, C11). OpenEval notes uncertainty about direct vs. indirect mechanism, while peer reviewers accept this as key mechanistic finding linking caspases to Notch. Agreement with acknowledged mechanistic uncertainty.

Both support that Wg, Dpp, and Hh signaling are not altered in emc mutants (C114-C115, C117, C119-C120). OpenEval details specific reporter experiments, while peer reviewers accept these as appropriate negative controls supporting Notch pathway specificity. Complete agreement.

Both support that Hedgehog/Ci signaling is not the primary mechanism (C127-C131, C133, C137, C139). OpenEval details Ci155 accumulation patterns and lack of correlation with furrow phenotype, while peer reviewers accept this as ruling out Hh signaling. Agreement despite complexity of data.

Both support that Da is elevated in all emc genotypes regardless of caspase status (C87-C88). OpenEval emphasizes this confirms emc null status and caspase-independence of Da regulation, while peer reviewers accept as appropriate control. Complete agreement.

Both support the overall mechanistic model involving Delta trans-activation and cis-inhibition (C184-C186, C12, C216-C217). OpenEval details how model is grounded in established Delta biology, while peer reviewers accept the caspase→Diap1→Delta→Notch pathway. Strong agreement on mechanistic framework.

Both strongly support the central conclusion that all four emc phenotypes are rescued by preventing caspase activation (C170-C171, C5, C198-C199, C206). OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive evidence across multiple rescue strategies, while peer reviewers describe work as 'compelling' and 'important.' Complete agreement on overarching conclusion.

Both acknowledge uncertainty about whether Delta is the direct caspase target (C182-C183). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN and notes computational predictions suggest cleavage would inactivate Delta, while peer reviewers accept this limitation as adequately defended. Agreement on uncertainty without undermining conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates clone boundary behavior and contrast with Su(H) clones (C160-C162, C164) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic interpretation is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about boundary smoothness.

OpenEval rates wing disc Diap1 findings (C95) as UNCERTAIN, noting potential tissue-specificity or technical limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this negative result in wing discs versus eye discs.

OpenEval evaluates that dronc single mutant clones grow normally (C73), contradicting prior literature. This is rated SUPPORTED as straightforward negative result. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this discrepancy with Verghese et al., 2012.
